s1.syndrome_frame: Acute neurological syndrome with fever and focal neurological deficits
salient_findings: High-grade fever for 14 days
Progressive weakness on the right side of body for 5 days
Upper motor neuron type right-sided seventh cranial-nerve palsy
Complete hemiplegia
Multifocal discrete and confluent hypodensities on brain CT
key_facts: Progressive weakness on the right side of body for 5 days
Upper motor neuron type right-sided seventh cranial-nerve palsy
Extensor plantar response on the right
SARS-CoV-2 RNA detected on nasopharyngeal swab by RT-PCR
CSF examination showed pleocytosis with slightly increased protein

shortlist.label: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Fits with acute neurological syndrome, fever, and focal neurological deficits

shortlist.label: Cerebral Vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Multifocal smooth stenosis of intracranial arteries and CSF pleocytosis support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Rasmussen Encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive hemiplegia and seizures are characteristic of this condition

shortlist.label: Moyamoya Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Multifocal stenosis of intracranial arteries and cerebral hypodensities are consistent with Moyamoya

shortlist.label: Herpes Simplex Encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Fever, headache, and focal neurological deficits are common in Herpes Simplex Encephalitis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including high-grade fever, throbbing headache, vomiting, progressive weakness, and upper motor neuron type right-sided seventh cranial-nerve palsy, along with the presence of multifocal discrete and confluent hypodensities in the brain CT and pleocytosis with slightly increased protein in the CSF examination, are consistent with Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis, especially given the recent SARS-CoV-2 infection which can trigger this condition.

rejected.label: Cerebral Vasculitis
rejected.why: While the patient has multifocal smooth stenosis of intracranial arteries, the overall clinical and laboratory picture, including the absence of specific vasculitis markers, does not strongly support this diagnosis as the primary explanation.

rejected.label: Rasmussen Encephalitis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with more chronic and progressive symptoms, particularly seizures, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Moyamoya Disease
rejected.why: The patient's age and the acute presentation do not align well with Moyamoya Disease, which often presents with more chronic symptoms and has a distinct angiographic pattern.

rejected.label: Herpes Simplex Encephalitis
rejected.why: The CSF examination did not specifically indicate the presence of herpes simplex virus, and the clinical presentation, although severe, does not strongly point towards this diagnosis without more specific evidence.
